rows.basis: total nickel content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)
rows.rationale: Nickel is the analyte this category's exposure pathway is built around: nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitiser, and a residue deposited on fabric that is then worn is prolonged, repeated dermal contact. No sovereign sets a nickel maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 — the instrument that anchors lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury on this row — sets no nickel limit at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit, which is the only regime in the register that sets one. The Korean instrument writes a product-form split (eye make-up 35, colour make-up 30, all other cosmetic products 10 mg/kg); the split is preserved and the "all other products" tier is the applicable one, because a fabric-care product is not a decorative make-up. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; the ASEAN, Health Canada and Germany BVL values are cosmetics-scoped administrative or technical-avoidability findings rather than statutory maximum levels, and are on-scope-only under governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL), and the same instrument is already the published read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move, verified 2026-08-17 against the live page https://heavymetalcertified.com/standards/all-purpose-cleaners (Category 12 standard version 1.0, dated 2026-08-13), which publishes lead 10, cadmium 5, total arsenic 2 and total mercury 1 mg/kg with provenance read-across and binding source China Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics (2015, NMPA), the values carried by register rows cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10, cn_nmpa2015_cd_cosmetics_5, cn_nmpa2015_tas_cosmetics_2 and cn_nmpa2015_thg_cosmetics_1, and which states the same single-coherent-regime rule; the Category 12 records were rendered by a dedicated certification-repository builder rather than through this repository's compiled-standards manifest, so the live page and not an in-repo artifact is the citation a reader checks. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restricts nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact rather than nickel content in a mixture and is not carried in the register as a content limit, so it is not read across; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 sets no nickel row for consumer textiles, so no downstream fabric content ceiling is available for this analyte. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Nickel is measured in soaps, detergents and household hygienic products in the routed corpus and is named for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp and ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 technical-avoidability findings for cosmetic manufacture, register status 'guidance impurity limit', dispositioned under HMTc governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL as on-scope-only and therefore unavailable as a read-across anchor for a non-cosmetic product class. The ruling is stated in full in this configuration's credible_note and is the single programme-wide rule the live Category 15 (Feminine Care) standard and this category both now state; Category 15 binds these same four BVL rows because its rows ARE cosmetics, and every number Category 15 publishes is unaffected by the ruling. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so nothing was excluded to make this list shorter. (4) Two further stricter rows exist that the compiler's audit safety-net structurally CANNOT surface, because it filters to the credible-regulator set, and they are therefore recorded by hand rather than left invisible. asean2019_th_cd_cosmetic_products_3000 (Thailand, cadmium 3 mg/kg) is a guidance impurity limit and falls to the same reasoning as the Health Canada value. eaeu_trcu009_2011_pb_natural_raw_material_cosmetics_5mgkg (EAEU, lead 5 mg/kg) is the only STATUTORY row anywhere in the consumer-chemical product-content basis family that is stricter than an anchor adopted here, and it is not adopted for three reasons: the EAEU is not in the HMTc credible-regulator set and admitting it is a governance ruling outside this derivation; its scope is formulation-conditioned (perfumery-cosmetic products containing more than 1 per cent natural plant or natural mineral raw material) rather than the general product tier, and that condition would be satisfied by some but not all rows in this category, which would fracture the category on a formulation test no sovereign wrote for laundry products; and the EAEU instrument does not dominate the adopted regime, since it is stricter on lead (5 against 10 mg/kg) but LOOSER on total arsenic (5 against 2 mg/kg), identical on mercury and silent on cadmium, so taking its lead value while keeping the Chinese arsenic value would compose a ceiling no sovereign enforces, which is precisely what the single-coherent-regime discipline exists to prevent. This enumeration is the output of a credible-set-blind sweep of every one of the 80 register rows the basis_guard admits, not of the automated scan alone, and it is complete as of this build. Verification method: total nickel by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of each functional phase and each physical component separately — the wash-active phase, the softening or protective phase, any nonwoven substrate, and any film, coating or wrapper — each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Disposition rule, stated identically in every cell and every row of this category: the published ceiling applies to EACH sampled component independently, and the lot fails if ANY single component result is at or above the ceiling. The whole-article composite is additionally measured and reported on the lot record, but the composite is never the basis of the pass or fail determination, because diluting a contaminated component in the mass of the rest of the article does not reduce the exposure that component delivers to the skin it contacts. A lot in which every component is inside the ceiling, but in which any component sits outside the running per-row control band, is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back to the specific component that moved.

rows.basis: total lead content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)
rows.rationale: Program-wide consistency ruling (2026-08-17): the German BVL 2017 orientation values are treated as SELECTABLE anchors across HMTc. The live Category 15 standard tags three of these same register rows regulatory-alignment, and Categories 2, 13, 14 and 20 bind them directly, so the earlier Category 19 position that a register status of 'guidance impurity limit' makes them unselectable contradicted five sibling categories on the identical rows, and did so in the looser direction (5x on lead, 50x on cadmium, 4x on total arsenic, 10x on total mercury). BVL is a single coherent sovereign consumer-chemical regime covering all four toxics, so reading it across preserves this category's own rule of adopting one coherent regime per analyte rather than picking the lowest number across regimes. The China NMPA 2015 value previously published is retained as a named looser comparator. Whether a national enforcement orientation value ranks as a sovereign maximum level is a genuine governance question, recorded for ratification as OI-20260817-bvl-selectability-ruling; until it is ruled on, every category states the same rule. Previously bound: cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10.

rows.basis: total nickel content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)
rows.rationale: Nickel is the analyte this category's exposure pathway is built around: nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitiser, and a residue deposited on fabric that is then worn is prolonged, repeated dermal contact. No sovereign sets a nickel maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 — the instrument that anchors lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury on this row — sets no nickel limit at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit, which is the only regime in the register that sets one. The Korean instrument writes a product-form split (eye make-up 35, colour make-up 30, all other cosmetic products 10 mg/kg); the split is preserved and the "all other products" tier is the applicable one, because a fabric-care product is not a decorative make-up. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; the ASEAN, Health Canada and Germany BVL values are cosmetics-scoped administrative or technical-avoidability findings rather than statutory maximum levels, and are on-scope-only under governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL), and the same instrument is already the published read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move, verified 2026-08-17 against the live page https://heavymetalcertified.com/standards/all-purpose-cleaners (Category 12 standard version 1.0, dated 2026-08-13), which publishes lead 10, cadmium 5, total arsenic 2 and total mercury 1 mg/kg with provenance read-across and binding source China Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics (2015, NMPA), the values carried by register rows cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10, cn_nmpa2015_cd_cosmetics_5, cn_nmpa2015_tas_cosmetics_2 and cn_nmpa2015_thg_cosmetics_1, and which states the same single-coherent-regime rule; the Category 12 records were rendered by a dedicated certification-repository builder rather than through this repository's compiled-standards manifest, so the live page and not an in-repo artifact is the citation a reader checks. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restricts nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact rather than nickel content in a mixture and is not carried in the register as a content limit, so it is not read across; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 sets no nickel row for consumer textiles, so no downstream fabric content ceiling is available for this analyte. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Nickel is measured in soaps, detergents and household hygienic products in the routed corpus and is named for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp and ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 technical-avoidability findings for cosmetic manufacture, register status 'guidance impurity limit', dispositioned under HMTc governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL as on-scope-only and therefore unavailable as a read-across anchor for a non-cosmetic product class. The ruling is stated in full in this configuration's credible_note and is the single programme-wide rule the live Category 15 (Feminine Care) standard and this category both now state; Category 15 binds these same four BVL rows because its rows ARE cosmetics, and every number Category 15 publishes is unaffected by the ruling. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so nothing was excluded to make this list shorter. (4) Two further stricter rows exist that the compiler's audit safety-net structurally CANNOT surface, because it filters to the credible-regulator set, and they are therefore recorded by hand rather than left invisible. asean2019_th_cd_cosmetic_products_3000 (Thailand, cadmium 3 mg/kg) is a guidance impurity limit and falls to the same reasoning as the Health Canada value. eaeu_trcu009_2011_pb_natural_raw_material_cosmetics_5mgkg (EAEU, lead 5 mg/kg) is the only STATUTORY row anywhere in the consumer-chemical product-content basis family that is stricter than an anchor adopted here, and it is not adopted for three reasons: the EAEU is not in the HMTc credible-regulator set and admitting it is a governance ruling outside this derivation; its scope is formulation-conditioned (perfumery-cosmetic products containing more than 1 per cent natural plant or natural mineral raw material) rather than the general product tier, and that condition would be satisfied by some but not all rows in this category, which would fracture the category on a formulation test no sovereign wrote for laundry products; and the EAEU instrument does not dominate the adopted regime, since it is stricter on lead (5 against 10 mg/kg) but LOOSER on total arsenic (5 against 2 mg/kg), identical on mercury and silent on cadmium, so taking its lead value while keeping the Chinese arsenic value would compose a ceiling no sovereign enforces, which is precisely what the single-coherent-regime discipline exists to prevent. This enumeration is the output of a credible-set-blind sweep of every one of the 80 register rows the basis_guard admits, not of the automated scan alone, and it is complete as of this build. Verification method: total nickel by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of every physical component and functional phase of the article, enumerated in the applicant's Step 0 scope determination and each sampled and tested as a distinct component; solid and sheet formats are separated into substrate and applied coating. Disposition rule, stated identically in every cell and every row of this category: the published ceiling applies to EACH sampled component independently, and the lot fails if ANY single component result is at or above the ceiling. The whole-article composite is additionally measured and reported on the lot record, but the composite is never the basis of the pass or fail determination, because diluting a contaminated component in the mass of the rest of the article does not reduce the exposure that component delivers to the skin it contacts. A lot in which every component is inside the ceiling, but in which any component sits outside the running per-row control band, is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back to the specific component that moved.

rows.basis: total nickel content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)
rows.rationale: Nickel is the analyte this category's exposure pathway is built around: nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitiser, and a residue deposited on fabric that is then worn is prolonged, repeated dermal contact. No sovereign sets a nickel maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 — the instrument that anchors lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury on this row — sets no nickel limit at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit, which is the only regime in the register that sets one. The Korean instrument writes a product-form split (eye make-up 35, colour make-up 30, all other cosmetic products 10 mg/kg); the split is preserved and the "all other products" tier is the applicable one, because a fabric-care product is not a decorative make-up. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; the ASEAN, Health Canada and Germany BVL values are cosmetics-scoped administrative or technical-avoidability findings rather than statutory maximum levels, and are on-scope-only under governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL), and the same instrument is already the published read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move, verified 2026-08-17 against the live page https://heavymetalcertified.com/standards/all-purpose-cleaners (Category 12 standard version 1.0, dated 2026-08-13), which publishes lead 10, cadmium 5, total arsenic 2 and total mercury 1 mg/kg with provenance read-across and binding source China Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics (2015, NMPA), the values carried by register rows cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10, cn_nmpa2015_cd_cosmetics_5, cn_nmpa2015_tas_cosmetics_2 and cn_nmpa2015_thg_cosmetics_1, and which states the same single-coherent-regime rule; the Category 12 records were rendered by a dedicated certification-repository builder rather than through this repository's compiled-standards manifest, so the live page and not an in-repo artifact is the citation a reader checks. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restricts nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact rather than nickel content in a mixture and is not carried in the register as a content limit, so it is not read across; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 sets no nickel row for consumer textiles, so no downstream fabric content ceiling is available for this analyte. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Nickel is measured in soaps, detergents and household hygienic products in the routed corpus and is named for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp and ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 technical-avoidability findings for cosmetic manufacture, register status 'guidance impurity limit', dispositioned under HMTc governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL as on-scope-only and therefore unavailable as a read-across anchor for a non-cosmetic product class. The ruling is stated in full in this configuration's credible_note and is the single programme-wide rule the live Category 15 (Feminine Care) standard and this category both now state; Category 15 binds these same four BVL rows because its rows ARE cosmetics, and every number Category 15 publishes is unaffected by the ruling. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so nothing was excluded to make this list shorter. (4) Two further stricter rows exist that the compiler's audit safety-net structurally CANNOT surface, because it filters to the credible-regulator set, and they are therefore recorded by hand rather than left invisible. asean2019_th_cd_cosmetic_products_3000 (Thailand, cadmium 3 mg/kg) is a guidance impurity limit and falls to the same reasoning as the Health Canada value. eaeu_trcu009_2011_pb_natural_raw_material_cosmetics_5mgkg (EAEU, lead 5 mg/kg) is the only STATUTORY row anywhere in the consumer-chemical product-content basis family that is stricter than an anchor adopted here, and it is not adopted for three reasons: the EAEU is not in the HMTc credible-regulator set and admitting it is a governance ruling outside this derivation; its scope is formulation-conditioned (perfumery-cosmetic products containing more than 1 per cent natural plant or natural mineral raw material) rather than the general product tier, and that condition would be satisfied by some but not all rows in this category, which would fracture the category on a formulation test no sovereign wrote for laundry products; and the EAEU instrument does not dominate the adopted regime, since it is stricter on lead (5 against 10 mg/kg) but LOOSER on total arsenic (5 against 2 mg/kg), identical on mercury and silent on cadmium, so taking its lead value while keeping the Chinese arsenic value would compose a ceiling no sovereign enforces, which is precisely what the single-coherent-regime discipline exists to prevent. This enumeration is the output of a credible-set-blind sweep of every one of the 80 register rows the basis_guard admits, not of the automated scan alone, and it is complete as of this build. Verification method: total nickel by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the finish concentrate and, for aerosol and trigger-spray formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. Disposition rule, stated identically in every cell and every row of this category: the published ceiling applies to EACH sampled component independently, and the lot fails if ANY single component result is at or above the ceiling. The whole-article composite is additionally measured and reported on the lot record, but the composite is never the basis of the pass or fail determination, because diluting a contaminated component in the mass of the rest of the article does not reduce the exposure that component delivers to the skin it contacts. A lot in which every component is inside the ceiling, but in which any component sits outside the running per-row control band, is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back to the specific component that moved.

rows.rationale: Program-wide consistency ruling (2026-08-17): the German BVL 2017 orientation values are treated as SELECTABLE anchors across HMTc. The live Category 15 standard tags three of these same register rows regulatory-alignment, and Categories 2, 13, 14 and 20 bind them directly, so the earlier Category 19 position that a register status of 'guidance impurity limit' makes them unselectable contradicted five sibling categories on the identical rows, and did so in the looser direction (5x on lead, 50x on cadmium, 4x on total arsenic, 10x on total mercury). BVL is a single coherent sovereign consumer-chemical regime covering all four toxics, so reading it across preserves this category's own rule of adopting one coherent regime per analyte rather than picking the lowest number across regimes. The China NMPA 2015 value previously published is retained as a named looser comparator. Whether a national enforcement orientation value ranks as a sovereign maximum level is a genuine governance question, recorded for ratification as OI-20260817-bvl-selectability-ruling; until it is ruled on, every category states the same rule. Previously bound: cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10.

rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for this exact form: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 2000 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 10000; Health Canada, 10000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 10000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 20000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 20000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 20000. Looser and therefore non-binding: the EAEU natural-raw-material tier (5000), the Korean clay-powder tier (50000), the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (20000 and 10000) and the Australian customs value (250000). The German value binds. Its own scope excludes the make-up categories the same table lists at 5000 ug/kg (make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up); none of those forms falls in this row, so the general branch is the applicable cell. The US FDA draft lead guidance for lip and externally applied cosmetics (10000) carries draft status in the register, is gated out by the compiler, and is looser in any case. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is neither an eye-makeup nor a colour-makeup product, so the 10000 ug/kg branch is the applicable cell and it binds. Where the mapping of an HMTc row onto the Korean product classes is not unambiguous, or where a row's forms straddle two branches, HMTc takes the stricter branch rather than claiming the looser one.

rows.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market — total element content per unit mass of undiluted product as sold (µg/kg). Not a dietary basis, not a migration or leachate basis, and no use-pattern dilution credit.
rows.rationale: BVL 2017 Table 1 (German Federal Office of Consumer Protection and Food Safety, with the Länder cosmetics working group) publishes the technically avoidable heavy-metal content of cosmetic products in general; lead is 2.0 mg/kg, and a content above the table is treated as technically avoidable under good manufacturing practice. Its status is a federal-authority guidance value rather than a statute, and it is disclosed as such, but it is the strictest published sovereign finished-cosmetic lead maximum and Method v2.0 takes the strictest applicable value. The named comparator set shows how far the binding sits below the field: Health Canada, China NMPA 2015 and Taiwan MOHW 2024 are five times looser at 10 mg/kg; Korea, ASEAN and its Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia transpositions, and Kenya KS 2937:2021 are ten times looser at 20 mg/kg; Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations threshold is 125 times looser at 250 mg/kg. Two sovereign cosmetic lead values in the register are stricter than the binding — the BVL 2017 toothpaste tier at 500 µg/kg and Washington State's Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act toothpaste limit at 1000 µg/kg — and the compiler's stricter-unselected audit flags both on every row of this category. Neither is applicable. Both are scoped by their own instruments to toothpaste, a dentifrice that sits on the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed; that ingestion pathway is the stated reason the toothpaste tier is tighter. Categories 20 and 2 carry the dentifrice forms and use those instruments. A shampoo, body wash, scrub or depilatory has no ingestion pathway inside either instrument's scope, so reading a toothpaste tier onto a hair or body rinse-off product would have HMTc inventing a stricter number that no government set for this form. Method v2.0 forbids that as squarely as it forbids inventing a looser one: applicability is a real constraint, and the strictest APPLICABLE value governs. The compiler's audit also flags EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75, which sets 700 µg/kg for lead in mixtures placed on the market for tattooing and permanent make-up. That value is stricter than the binding and is deliberately not adopted: the instrument governs a mixture INJECTED INTO THE DERMIS, on a 'mixture for tattooing or permanent make-up by weight' basis, and a rinse-off shampoo or body wash is not such a mixture on any reading of the entry. The row is held out by this row's basis_guard as well as on scope. It is surfaced rather than filtered out of the scan so that the record shows it was found and disposed of, not missed. Colour-additive and colourant purity specifications (21 CFR 73 and 74, the New Zealand and Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles, the India Cosmetics Rules 2020 permitted-colours entries, the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant entries) are raw-material ingredient specifications, not finished-product maxima. They are held out of every cell by this row's basis_guard, and none of them is in any case stricter than the binding for this analyte.

Mercury used as an intentional skin-lightening active, and the eye-area thiomersal and phenylmercuric preservative allowances in the India, Hong Kong and South Africa instruments, are ingredient permissions rather than contaminant ceilings; HMTc does not adopt them, and a rinse-off product formulated with an intentional mercury ingredient is not certifiable at all. Colour-additive and colourant purity specifications (21 CFR 73 and 74, the New Zealand and Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles, the India Cosmetics Rules 2020 permitted-colours entries, the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant entries) are raw-material ingredient specifications, not finished-product maxima. rows.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market — total element content per unit mass of undiluted product as sold (µg/kg). Not a dietary basis, not a migration or leachate basis, and no use-pattern dilution credit.
rows.rationale: Korea is the only jurisdiction in the register that sets a nickel content limit for finished cosmetics, and it tiers it by form: 10 µg/g for cosmetic products other than eye makeup and colour cosmetics, 30 µg/g for colour makeup, 35 µg/g for eye makeup. Every Category 14 form is a cleansing, conditioning, shaving, depilatory or hair-colouring preparation and none is an eye-makeup or colour-makeup product in the MFDS product taxonomy, so the strictest of the three tiers — 10 µg/g — is the directly applicable one, not a read-across. Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 carries the same 10 µg/g value for the same scope and corroborates it; it is not named as a candidate because its register note contradicts its own value (the note reads '1 microgram/g = 1000 ug/kg' against a stored value of 10000 µg/kg), and a litigation-facing citation should not carry that discrepancy forward. The EU REACH restriction on nickel in tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures (5000 µg/kg) is stricter but governs a mixture injected into the dermis, a different form on a different basis, and is held out by this row's basis_guard. Nickel is a leading contact sensitiser, so the programme additionally holds it under ALARA post-publication and treats the published ceiling as an outer bound rather than a target.

rows.basis: as consumed, ready-to-drink fermented beverage (read across from the Hong Kong wine cell)
rows.rationale: The candidate set and the rejections, stated plainly because this is the cell most open to attack. The audit scan flags the entire juice and nectar lead family as stricter and unselected: the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg), the Hong Kong grape-juice cell (40 ug/kg), the EU and Hong Kong berry and small-fruit juice cells (50 ug/kg) and the US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level (50 ug/kg). All were considered and all are rejected on the same two grounds: a finished ferment is not a fruit juice, a juice from concentrate or a nectar within those instruments' scope, and fermentation is precisely the step that changes the matrix and opens the equipment-leaching route, so an unfermented-input cell does not describe the certified product. The packaged-drinking-water standards (5 to 10 ug/kg) govern water sold as water. That leaves the Wine cell, which is a genuine sovereign value for a fermented fruit beverage in the identical as-consumed basis. HMTc adopts it for the ferments this row certifies and does not conceal two things about it. It is weak: because the acid ferment sits against equipment for weeks, this cell carries mandatory lot testing with an equipment and closure investigation on any result above 30 ug/kg, and it is a declared Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12. And it is drawn from a pool the register is known to be missing entries from: the EU 2023/915 wine, cider, perry and fruit-wine lead cells are not in the register, their absence is logged as a register gap, and it is filled neither by an occurrence value nor by recollection of the instrument. That gap is why wine, cider, perry and beer are excluded from this row's scope rather than certified against 200 ug/kg, and it also qualifies this read-across for the forms that remain: if any of the missing cells is stricter than 200 ug/kg it becomes the nearest applicable sovereign value for a fermented beverage and supersedes this anchor at the next recompilation. Until then the read-across is published with that qualification on its face rather than as a settled ceiling.

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for wine, cider, beer or any other fermented beverage; the only cadmium values for fermented drinks anywhere in the register are non-credible-tier wine cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay at 10 ug/kg), which sit outside the credible-regulator set and were not used. The absence of a credible cadmium cell for fermented beverages is reported as a regulatory gap. rows.basis: wet weight, ready-to-drink beverage (read across from the EU fruit-juice inorganic-arsenic cell)
rows.rationale: Beverage-to-beverage read-across with no basis change, adopted in the strict direction. Unlike lead, arsenic has no equipment-leaching route that fermentation opens up: it arrives with the water, the fruit or grain substrate and any added mineral salts, and an aqueous beverage cell at 20 ug/kg describes that route. Non-credible-tier fermented-beverage arsenic cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay wine at 200 ug/kg total arsenic) are far looser and outside the credible set.

rows.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
rows.rationale: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a non-tea fermented beverage. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 2.5 to 3.8 after fermentation, with lactic, acetic, citric and malic acid and residual sugars present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.

rows.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the US bottled-water quality standard)
rows.rationale: A flavoured water is, compositionally, packaged drinking water plus a flavour dose, and it is sold and consumed as water; the packaged-water quality standard is therefore the nearest applicable sovereign cell in an identical aqueous as-consumed basis. The competing candidate was the Hong Kong carbonated-beverage lead cell (200 ug/kg), which does directly cover a sparkling flavoured water as a carbonated beverage. Both are applicable to forms in this row, so Method v2.0 step 3 compels the strictest applicable value, and that is 5 ug/kg, not 200. Adopting 200 here would have been the convenience choice and is expressly rejected: a product that is 99 percent water cannot be held to a ceiling forty times the standard its own water base must already meet. The scope note draws the boundary that makes this defensible, excluding formulated beverages from the row.

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a packaged water or a flavoured water; the packaged-water instruments cap arsenic as an unspeciated total, and this row adopts that total at 10 ug/kg. Publishing a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would either duplicate the total (adding nothing) or exceed it (an impossibility, since iAs <= tAs by identity), so the honest disposition is a control bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling rather than an invented species number. This is a control and not a not-material determination because inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant species in an aqueous matrix and is genuinely present in groundwater-sourced water: the analyte is real, only the separate ceiling is unavailable.

rows.basis: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
rows.rationale: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: the filament or yarn (PTFE, nylon or silk), the wax, flavour or fluoride coating on it, the interdental brush wire and its polymer coating, the pick or handle polymer, any wooden or bamboo stick, and any accessible metal cutter on the dispenser. The coating is sampled separately from the filament because flavour, wax and fluoride coatings carry their own mineral and pigment inputs and would be diluted below detection in a whole-product composite. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

rows.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
rows.rationale: The exact cell is unregulated: the food-contact surface of a food can is a cured organic coating, and coatings and varnishes are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, while Regulation (EU) 10/2011 reaches plastic layers and plastic coatings in multi-material multi-layer articles but is not written for a liquid-applied cured lacquer. The nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical basis is therefore the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact layer, and it is read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. Applied to the can, this ceiling governs the lacquered interior surface as the food-contact surface; the uncoated-tinplate and breached-coating configurations are handled by the component plan under the metal-article release control regime, and the tin pathway is a control on every configuration. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

PROVENANCE NOTE: this cell is tagged READ-ACROSS rather than regulatory-alignment because this taxonomy row covers two material configurations. The uncoated paperboard in direct food contact is a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I paper-and-board material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure and for which no credible sovereign sets an element migration ceiling, so for that configuration the exact cell is unregulated and the identical value is applied as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS holding the basis constant: the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in ug/kg of food, determined by the same test conventions. The published number is the same for both configurations, so nothing is loosened. The conservative tag is used so that the machine-readable provenance never asserts regulatory alignment to an instrument whose own scope article does not reach one of this row's materials; splitting the row in two, each with its own provenance, is recorded as a taxonomy change for governance.

rows.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
rows.rationale: Aluminium carries a positive specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, added by Reg (EU) 2016/1416. The food-contact layer is a plastic layer in a multi-material multi-layer article, which this instrument governs directly under Art. 2(1)(c); the uncoated-board configuration takes the same values by disclosed read-across. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface; it is not applied to an aluminium metal article, because an instrument written for plastics did not contemplate an article whose food-contact surface is the element itself. PROVENANCE NOTE: this cell is tagged READ-ACROSS rather than regulatory-alignment because this taxonomy row covers two material configurations. The polymer-coated and laminated carton, whose food-contact surface is an inner polyolefin layer in a multi-material multi-layer material and is governed by the instrument directly under Art. 2(1)(c) is within the instrument's direct scope, and for that configuration the value is a direct sovereign maximum. The uncoated paperboard in direct food contact is a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I paper-and-board material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure and for which no credible sovereign sets an element migration ceiling, so for that configuration the exact cell is unregulated and the identical value is applied as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS holding the basis constant: the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in ug/kg of food, determined by the same test conventions. The published number is the same for both configurations, so nothing is loosened. The conservative tag is used so that the machine-readable provenance never asserts regulatory alignment to an instrument whose own scope article does not reach one of this row's materials; splitting the row in two, each with its own provenance, is recorded as a taxonomy change for governance.

rows.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
rows.rationale: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. The bowl and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the stainless cutting components are reported under the alloy-release regime in the component plan.

rows.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
rows.rationale: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

rows.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
rows.rationale: The exact cell is unregulated by construction rather than by omission: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Art. 2(2)(c) expressly excludes silicones from its scope, and no EU specific measure and no other credible sovereign instrument sets an element migration ceiling for a silicone food-contact article. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the EU 10/2011 Annex II element requirement for a polymeric food-contact material, read across with disclosure. The read-across holds the basis constant: source and destination are the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in µg/kg food, determined by the same test conventions. The analogy is on basis and exposure endpoint, not on material identity, and it is disclosed as a read-across rather than presented as a limit written for this article. Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. The read-across is tight here: source and destination are both synthetic-polymer repeat-use food-contact articles tested by the same simulant conventions, and the only difference is that the destination polymer was carved out of the instrument's scope for reasons unrelated to element migration. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for this exact form: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 2000 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 10000; Health Canada, 10000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 10000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 20000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 20000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 20000. Looser and therefore non-binding: the EAEU natural-raw-material tier (5000), the Korean clay-powder tier (50000), the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (20000 and 10000) and the Australian customs value (250000). The German value binds. Its own scope excludes the make-up categories the same table lists at 5000 ug/kg (make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up); none of those forms falls in this row, so the general branch is the applicable cell. The US FDA draft lead guidance for lip and externally applied cosmetics (10000) carries draft status in the register, is gated out by the compiler, and is looser in any case. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is neither an eye-makeup nor a colour-makeup product, so the 10000 ug/kg branch is the applicable cell and it binds. Where the mapping of an HMTc row onto the Korean product classes is not unambiguous, or where a row's forms straddle two branches, HMTc takes the stricter branch rather than claiming the looser one.

rows.basis: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
rows.rationale: Direct maximum levels for the exact product form in the row's native basis. The berry and cranberry rows at 200 ug/kg are the government-written carve-outs for the accumulating small-fruit species; because one HMTc value must hold across the whole row, the row binds 100 ug/kg and cranberry, currant and elderberry products certify against a value stricter than their own sovereign class. The AU-NZ row is applied on the fresh basis only; Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis, which is why it is not carried into the dried-fruit row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS (from the broader register review rather than this row's scan, which returned no stricter-unselected rows): two stricter Hong Kong rows exist that are not applicable to fresh fruit. 'Tomatoes, preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed' (50 ug/kg) is a heat-sterilised canned tomato product and routes to Category 32 tomato-condiments. 'Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree' (50 ug/kg) is a canned tree-nut product and routes to Category 28. MERCOSUR and Paraguayan 'fruit-based ice cream' rows (lead 70 ug/kg, cadmium 50 ug/kg, total arsenic 100 ug/kg) are a frozen dessert form and are not fresh fruit. FROZEN-DESSERT DISPOSITION (identical wording is used in the fruit-snacks lead and total-arsenic cells, the only other places this category states it): fruit-based ice cream and other frozen desserts are out of scope for Category 4 and NO taxonomy row anywhere in hmtc-v2.json currently receives them. Category 24 (Dairy and Milk Products) has nine subcategories (cow milk; goat/sheep/other ruminant milk; camel milk; cheese; yogurt and cultured dairy; cream; milk powders; condensed and evaporated milks; butter and ghee) and contains no ice-cream or frozen-dessert row, so any statement that these products route to Category 24 is false. The lead and total-arsenic rows are stricter than the fruit-snacks row's published values and are currently orphaned, covered by no HMTc standard; this is logged as an open, human-gated taxonomy gap (a new frozen-dessert subcategory carrying the MERCOSUR and Paraguayan fruit_based_ice_cream lead, cadmium and total-arsenic rows) rather than resolved by sweeping a frozen dessert into a produce row whose basis and product form it does not share.

rows.basis: as_sold

rows.rationale: This is a direct regulatory lookup, not a calculation. The candidate set deliberately includes the looser government-written splits so the selection is auditable: grape juice at 40 ug/kg (Codex and Hong Kong) and juices exclusively from berries and other small fruits at 50 ug/kg (EU 2023/915 section 3.1.19.1 and Hong Kong), plus the older US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level of 50 ug/kg. Because the whole apple-containing juice family is certified as a single row, the row ceiling is the strictest applicable value across every form in scope, 30 ug/kg. That is deliberate over-compliance for grape and berry juices relative to their own government-written cells, and it is disclosed here rather than buried: a grape or berry juice that meets 40 or 50 ug/kg is lawful in the EU, Codex and Hong Kong but is not HMTc-certifiable in this row. The US FDA 2022 draft action levels for lead in juice (10 ug/kg for single-strength apple juice, 20 ug/kg for other single-strength juices and blends) are DRAFT guidance expressly not for implementation and are therefore not eligible anchors; they are recorded so that the register's gated draft rows are visibly accounted for rather than silently omitted.

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in single-strength apple juice or an apple-containing juice blend. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 3.3 to 4.0, with malic and ascorbic acid present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.

rows.basis: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice; a concentrate is assessed as reconstituted to the original juice concentration, which is the basis the instruments themselves write
rows.rationale: This is a direct regulatory lookup, not a calculation. The candidate set deliberately includes the looser government-written splits so the selection is auditable: grape juice at 40 ug/kg (Codex and Hong Kong) and juices exclusively from berries and other small fruits at 50 ug/kg (EU 2023/915 section 3.1.19.1 and Hong Kong), plus the older US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level of 50 ug/kg. Because the whole non-apple fruit-juice family is certified as a single row, the row ceiling is the strictest applicable value across every form in scope, 30 ug/kg. That is deliberate over-compliance for grape and berry juices relative to their own government-written cells, and it is disclosed here rather than buried: a grape or berry juice that meets 40 or 50 ug/kg is lawful in the EU, Codex and Hong Kong but is not HMTc-certifiable in this row. The US FDA 2022 draft action levels for lead in juice (10 ug/kg for single-strength apple juice, 20 ug/kg for other single-strength juices and blends) are DRAFT guidance expressly not for implementation and are therefore not eligible anchors; they are recorded so that the register's gated draft rows are visibly accounted for rather than silently omitted.

The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a single-strength fruit juice. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 3.0 to 4.0, with citric, malic and ascorbic acid present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.

rows.basis: manufactured fruit snack as offered to the consumer
rows.rationale: R1 direct maximum level for the manufactured product class in the row's own basis. MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 write 300 ug/kg for compotes, jellies, jams, marmalades and other fruit or vegetable sweets. Israel MOH FCS-2016 is looser for this analyte in both of its applicable categories (residual fruits and vegetables 1000 ug/kg; dried fruits and vegetables 5000 ug/kg), so it does not bind here, which is why this cell does not name the Israeli rows that bind the lead, cadmium, inorganic-arsenic and total-mercury cells of the same row. Total arsenic is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; both are reported, and the inorganic-arsenic species value of 60 ug/kg is the operative arsenic constraint for this row. AUDIT DISPOSITION: the scan surfaces MERCOSUR and Paraguayan 'fruit-based ice cream' total arsenic at 100 ug/kg. FROZEN-DESSERT DISPOSITION (single wording used in every place this category states it): fruit-based ice cream and other frozen desserts are OUT OF SCOPE for this row and for Category 4 as a whole, and NO taxonomy row anywhere in hmtc-v2.json currently receives them. Category 24 (Dairy and Milk Products) has nine subcategories (cow milk; goat/sheep/other ruminant milk; camel milk; cheese; yogurt and cultured dairy; cream; milk powders; condensed and evaporated milks; butter and ghee) and contains no ice-cream or frozen-dessert row, so the earlier statement that these products 'route to Category 24' was false and has been removed. The consequence is recorded rather than buried: mercosur_gmc12_2011_fruit_based_ice_cream_pb_70 and py_decreto1335_2019_fruit_based_ice_cream_pb_70 (lead 70 ug/kg), the matching cadmium rows at 50 ug/kg, and mercosur_gmc12_2011_fruit_based_ice_cream_tas_100 with its Paraguayan twin (total arsenic 100 ug/kg) are STRICTER than this row's published lead and total-arsenic values and are currently orphaned, covered by no HMTc standard. This is logged as an open, human-gated taxonomy gap (a new frozen-dessert subcategory carrying those MERCOSUR and Paraguayan rows) and is not resolved by silently sweeping the frozen form into a produce row whose basis and product form it does not share.

rows.basis: as_sold
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form, and no not-material determination is supportable for it: the routed corpus quantifies methylmercury in edible plant and fungal tissue (wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china measured methylmercury in the leaf and root tissue of an edible leafy vegetable at an LOD of 0.002 ug/kg; stasinos2014-heavy-metals-tubers-review in root and tuber tissue; asensio2023-madrid-mushrooms-mercury), so the species is not absent from produce and the biological premise of a not-material determination is rebutted inside this very category. This row is a manufactured derivative of the fresh commodity, whose own methylmercury cell is held under the same control; a manufactured derivative is never granted a weaker determination than the fresh row it derives from. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3, 30 ug/kg); methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury. No methylmercury ceiling is invented.

rows.basis: as sold, edible portion (wet weight)
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign government names venison, bison, wild boar, rabbit or hare in a lead maximum level: the credible instruments enumerate cattle, sheep, goat, pig and poultry. The exact cell is therefore unregulated and the nearest applicable sovereign cell is the domestic-mammal muscle-meat lead maximum level, adopted by disclosed read-across at 0.1 mg/kg. Two independent credible instruments carry that same value (Hong Kong Cap. 132V meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep; FSANZ Schedule 19 meat of cattle, sheep, pig and poultry), which is why no looser figure is defensible. The looser edible-offal lead maximum levels (0.15-0.5 mg/kg) are a different scope and are deliberately NOT adopted even though wild game is a lead-exposed animal: the ammunition pathway is a reason for stricter surveillance, never a reason to widen the ceiling. Certified lots must be screened for metallic lead fragments by radiography or equivalent before grinding, and a fragment finding is a hard stop for the batch irrespective of the assayed mean.
