rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Applicable sovereign maxima surveyed for this exact form: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic orientation value, 2000 ug/kg; China NMPA 2015, 10000; Health Canada, 10000; Taiwan MOHW 2024, 10000; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, 20000; Singapore HSA 2024 and the ASEAN directive with its Indonesian and Malaysian transpositions, 20000; Kenya KS 2937:2021, 20000. Looser and therefore non-binding: the EAEU natural-raw-material tier (5000), the Korean clay-powder tier (50000), the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (20000 and 10000) and the Australian customs value (250000). The German value binds. Its own scope excludes the make-up categories the same table lists at 5000 ug/kg (make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up); none of those forms falls in this row, so the general branch is the applicable cell. The US FDA draft lead guidance for lip and externally applied cosmetics (10000) carries draft status in the register, is gated out by the compiler, and is looser in any case. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is neither an eye-makeup nor a colour-makeup product, so the 10000 ug/kg branch is the applicable cell and it binds. Where the mapping of an HMTc row onto the Korean product classes is not unambiguous, or where a row's forms straddle two branches, HMTc takes the stricter branch rather than claiming the looser one.

rows.basis: as sold, dry matcha powder
rows.rationale: Direct regulatory lookup: matcha is Camellia sinensis leaf, ground rather than left whole, and no credible instrument writes a separate cell for the ground form, so the commodity cell applies as written. The consequence is disclosed rather than smoothed: because matcha is ingested whole, a lot at the 5000 ug/kg ceiling delivers the full leaf lead burden to the consumer, where an infusion made from leaf at the same ceiling would deliver only the extractable fraction and Hong Kong's own beverage cell would cap the resulting drink at 200 ug/kg. HMTc does not resolve that asymmetry by inventing an extraction-corrected number, which Method v2.0 forbids; it publishes the government value, flags the whole-leaf ingestion route on the certificate, and treats this cell as a first-order Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12, where certified-lot evidence is the only admissible basis for a lower value.

The EU Drinking Water Directive value is not used on this row because the Directive excludes natural mineral water from its scope. rows.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
rows.rationale: Cadmium at 2 µg/L is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value (0.002 mg/L, nhmrc2025_cd_drinking_water_2), the strictest cadmium value any government sets for water. It is published as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS and not as a direct maximum for this product form, and the reason is stated rather than left to inference. The register records that instrument's product scope as 'drinking water' and its note describes it as a health-based guideline value; the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines are a non-statutory guideline for drinking-water supplies, and Australia regulates packaged water not under the ADWG but under the FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code. No FSANZ packaged-water metals row exists in the register: of the AU, NZ and AU-NZ rows, the only water-scoped entries are the eight NHMRC drinking-water guideline values, and Schedule 19 is represented only by commodity rows (formula, cereals, fish, salt and the like). The Australian packaged-water cadmium cell is therefore absent from the register and is logged as a register gap, in the same way Commission Directive 2003/40/EC is logged on the mineral-water row. The category's two textual packaged-water bridges do not carry this instrument either: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA maximum contaminant levels (cadmium 5 µg/L) and EU Directive 2020/2184's scope reaches water put into bottles or containers (cadmium 5 µg/L), and neither reaches an Australian guideline. Absence of a packaged-product carve-out is not affirmative scope, so the earlier regulatory-alignment tag overstated what this instrument does. WHAT THE INSTRUMENTS SET FOR THE EXACT CELL IS STATED OPENLY, because the read-across runs in the protective direction and nothing is served by concealing it: the strictest maximum level any government sets for cadmium in this exact packaged-water form is 3 µg/L, then 5 µg/L (EU Drinking Water Directive eu20202184_cd_drinking_water_5, FDA 21 CFR 165.110 fda21cfr165110_cd_bottled_water_5, EPA MCL epa2018_cd_drinking_water_5, California us_ca_swrcb_2024_cd_cadmium_mcl_5ugl), then 7 µg/L (Health Canada healthcanada2025_cd_drinking_water_7). HMTc publishes the stricter 2 µg/L: the substance and the basis are identical, HMTc does not relax a published limit toward a looser instrument, and the value is unchanged from the earlier compilation. Only the provenance tag is corrected, from regulatory-alignment to read-across, so that the record never claims a sovereign packaged-water maximum that no sovereign has written. The mineral-water-specific lines cluster at 3 µg/L (Hong Kong Cap 132V hk_cap132v_cd_natural-mineral-waters_3, India FSSAI 2016 in_fssai2016_cd_014_natural_mineral_water_3, GSO 193/2021 gso193_2021_cd_natural_mineral_waters_3, Colombia Res 4506/2013 co_res4506_2013_cd_mineral_water_3, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 vn_qcvn8_2_2011_cd_natural-mineral-water_3, Israel FCS 2016 il_fcs2016_cd_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_3), with Fiji FSR 2009 at 5 µg/L and Chile Decreto 977/1996 at 10 µg/L. Cadmium is a contaminant, not a characterising mineral constituent, so nothing in the natural-mineral-water product definition makes the stricter drinking-water value inapplicable. REGISTER GAP ON THIS CELL: Commission Directive 2003/40/EC, the EU instrument that sets metals limits for natural mineral waters, is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv and is therefore absent from this cell's candidate set; it is logged as a register gap and no value is asserted for it.

rows.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. The drinking-water instrument family carries no tin parameter at all (EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts B and C; US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110 standards of quality; Health Canada; NHMRC; WHO), and none of the national food-schedule packaged-water lines (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009) carries a tin entry for water. A read-across is not supportable: the nearest sovereign tin maxima are the canned-food and canned-beverage maximum levels, which exist to bound dissolution of tin from a tinplate container wall into an acidic canned matrix, and the canned-beverage value (100 mg/kg inorganic tin) sits roughly four orders of magnitude above anything a packaged water can plausibly contain, so importing it would publish a ceiling that functions as no limit at all. The dominant packaging for this category (PET, HDPE, glass, aluminium) contains no tin. Natural mineral water is bottled at source in glass or PET; tinplate presentation does not occur in this form. Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.

rows.rationale: The exact cell is unregulated, and the record says so on its face rather than asserting a maximum no government has written for this product form. No jurisdiction in the register sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for bottled water, packaged water or natural mineral water, and neither of the two textual packaged-water bridges this category relies on reaches the species: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation maximum contaminant levels and EPA sets no hexavalent-chromium MCL, and EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I carries no hexavalent-chromium parameter. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 Table 64431-A maximum contaminant level of 10 µg/L (0.01 mg/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl), re-adopted in 2024 after health-risk and feasibility analysis, and it is carried across as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS. Two hops are disclosed rather than argued around. First, SCOPE: the register records that instrument's product scope as 'public water systems in California', which is utility-delivered tap water and not a packaged good; HMTc has not identified, and does not cite, any California provision applying Title 22 section 64431 maximum contaminant levels to bottled water sold in the state, so this cell must not be read as an assertion that California enforces 10 µg/L against a packaged product. Second, SOVEREIGNTY: California is a sub-national government. The only alternative anywhere in the register is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines statement that hexavalent chromium should not exceed 50 µg/L (nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50), which is five times looser and carries the same drinking-water scope hop; it is named here and not selected because the method takes the strictest applicable value. The value is unchanged from the earlier compilation at 10 µg/L; only the provenance tag is corrected, from regulatory-alignment to read-across. HMTc publishes Cr-VI as its own cell in addition to total chromium: a hexavalent result never satisfies the total-chromium cell and a total-chromium result never satisfies this one, and the total-chromium cell on this row is a direct sovereign maximum for the product form that bounds this species from above. Neither named instrument carves natural mineral water out of its own scope, but neither reaches packaged water of any kind, which is why this cell is a read-across on this row for the same reason it is one on the other three.

rows.basis: read-across from strictest applicable principal-component Pb ML (as consumed)
rows.rationale: THE BINDING MOVED IN v1.2 BECAUSE THE DAIRY EXCLUSION DID NOT SURVIVE AUDIT. The ruling, the test that produced it, and the rejected alternatives are stated in full in this row's scope_note; in short, no mass or characterizing test distinguishes cream in a bisque or cheese in a macaroni-and-cheese from the seafood, meat and vegetable components already imported, so hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 are admitted and the ceiling is 20 ug/kg. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a meal whose characterizing component is a cereal (Cap. 132V and FSANZ cereal lead 200) or a fish (EU 300) contains a component whose own sovereign ceiling is up to fifteen times this composite ceiling, so such a product may measure above it. That does not loosen the ceiling; the component is governed at its own stage by its own category, and a composite lot above 20 ug/kg lead is not certifiable on this row. The v1.1 ladder is retained and unchanged below the new binding: Cap. 132V sets lead at 50 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables (cucurbit and non-cucurbit alike) and for tomatoes preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed, which is the canned tomato base of most sauced prepared meals. Two stricter Cap. 132V lead rows remain deliberately NOT adopted and are now equal to rather than stricter than the binding: cereal-based food (20 ug/kg) and ready-to-eat complementary food other than cereal-based (20 ug/kg), both scoped to persons under the age of 36 months. This row certifies adult and general-population meals only; infant and toddler mixed meals route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule, so an under-36-months action level is not an applicable anchor here, and the Codex ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children ML (20 ug/kg) is dispositioned identically. Leafy-vegetable lead MLs (EU 2023/915 and Cap. 132V, 300 ug/kg each) and the fish ML (300) are applicable but looser and are disclosed rather than adopted. BEVERAGE-COMMODITY RULING, applied once and consistently across every analyte on this row. Fruit and vegetable juices, nectars, rice-based drinks, and bottled and packaged waters are separately regulated ready-to-drink beverage commodities, consumed as the whole product, and they are NOT principal components of a prepared meal, soup, broth or stock. Where a formulation contains juice or juice concentrate it enters as a minor flavour, sweetener or acidulant fraction of a few percent, exactly like the cooking fat and the salt this row already dispositions as ingredient specifications rather than composite ceilings, and the vegetable commodity that a vegetable juice is pressed from is already in the ladder at its own maximum level (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), so adopting the juice row as well would import the same commodity twice in a form this row does not sell. The rows dispositioned by this ruling, named by id so the choice is auditable: eu2024_ni_juice_250 (nickel 250, fruit/vegetable juices and nectars) and eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000 (nickel 1000); fda2023_ias_apple_juice_10 (inorganic arsenic 10, apple juice), eu2023_ias_fruit_juice_20 (inorganic arsenic 20) and eu2023_ias_rice_drinks_30 (inorganic arsenic 30, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks); eu2023_pb_fruit_juice_other_30, hk_cap132v_pb_fruit-juices-other-than-fruit-juices-exclusively-from-b_30 and hk_cap132v_pb_grape-juice_40 (lead 30 to 40); and the packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values dispositioned in the row scope note. THE RULING IS TESTED BY ITS CONSEQUENCE: if a juice were a principal component, the US apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg would become the ceiling for an entire prepared meal, which no sovereign anywhere has set and which would be an occurrence-free but nonsensical import. Adopting the nickel juice row at 250 while declining the inorganic-arsenic juice row at 10 is the asymmetry this remediation exists to remove, so both are declined under one stated rule. v1.2 REMOVES juice, nectar and drink from this row's audit_exclude_scope so these rows now surface in the compiler's stricter-unselected scan and in the publication gate's W1 warnings, where they are dispositioned by this paragraph rather than suppressed by a regex. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant lead row below 20 ug/kg returns only drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (5 to 10 ug/kg) and the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), both refused by this row's basis_guard as different basis families. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

rows.basis: read-across from strictest applicable principal-component Cd ML (as consumed)
rows.rationale: INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

rows.basis: read-across from strictest applicable principal-component total-arsenic ML (as consumed)
rows.rationale: TOTAL ARSENIC IS PUBLISHED HERE AS A PROTECTIVE SOVEREIGN MAXIMUM LEVEL, NOT AS A SCREEN. v1.1 opened this substantiation with 'Total arsenic is a non-toxicological screen' while the cell emitted an ordinary numeric read-across with no screen flag, so the prose and the provenance disagreed about whether the published number was protective and any renderer that distinguishes the two would have contradicted the cell's own text. The disagreement is resolved in favour of what the cell in fact publishes: Cap. 132V regulates total arsenic as a per-commodity protective ceiling, 500 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum level for the components of this row, and it is published as such. Total arsenic is one of the eight mandatory HMTc totals and is never satisfied by its species. The screen mechanism (`screen: true` with a screen_note) is used on this config only for total chromium, where the published value genuinely is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling; it is not available on a component_read_across cell in this compiler in any case. The toxicologically dominant arsenic species, inorganic arsenic, is separately and far more strictly controlled on the iAs cell at 50 ug/kg (EU 2025/1891 cephalopods), and the species-below-total relation holds (iAs 50 <= tAs 500). v1.1 tightens the cell from 1000 to 500 ug/kg because the Cap. 132V per-commodity total-arsenic MLs reach the components for which the FSANZ cereal-grain ML was the only anchor, and the v1.0 claim that cereal grains carry the only credible total-arsenic component ML is withdrawn. Rice is deliberately absent from Cap. 132V's total-arsenic schedule because rice is regulated on inorganic arsenic instead; that is handled on the iAs cell and never by letting a species stand in for a total. The Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils total-arsenic ML (100 ug/kg) is stricter still and is NOT adopted: cooking fat is a minor formulation ingredient rather than a characterizing component of a meal, edible oils certify under HMTc Category 30 in their own basis, and holding a whole meal to an oil ceiling would import a limit from a material that is a few percent of the product. Food-grade salt (500) is dispositioned the same way, as an ingredient specification rather than a composite ceiling. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant total-arsenic row below 500 ug/kg returns drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (10) and the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), both refused by this row's basis_guard; and us_fda_21cfr73_73_520_tas_50 at 50, which is a colour-additive ingredient specification for soy leghemoglobin under 21 CFR 73.520, a purity specification for an additive as supplied rather than a contaminant ceiling for a food as sold, dispositioned in the same form as the edible-fats-and-oils and salt rows below. rows.basis: read-across from strictest applicable inorganic-arsenic component ML (as consumed)
rows.rationale: THE FULL EU 2025/1891 SEAFOOD INORGANIC-ARSENIC LADDER, disclosed because the row previously named one rung of it and carried no substantiation at all: cephalopods 50 (eu20251891_ias_cephalopods_50); muscle meat of fish other than the listed species 100 (eu20251891_ias_fish_other_100), crabs and crab-like crustaceans, prawns and shrimps 100 (eu20251891_ias_crabs_prawns_shrimps_100) and scallops 100 (eu20251891_ias_scallops_100), three equal-value applicable candidates; crustaceans other than those listed 200 (eu20251891_ias_crustaceans_other_200); muscle meat of anglerfish, monkfish and the other listed species 500 (eu20251891_ias_fish_listed_500) and bivalve molluscs other than scallops 500 (eu20251891_ias_bivalve_molluscs_other_500); and langoustine and rock lobster 1500 (eu20251891_ias_langoustine_rock_lobster_1500). CEPHALOPODS ARE ADOPTED and the published ceiling moves from 100 to 50 ug/kg. They are a principal seafood component of products this row certifies, and the row says so in its own voice elsewhere: the component label reads fish/seafood rather than fish, and the total-mercury substantiation names prawn stir-fry, clam chowder and lobster bisque as covered products, so aquatic invertebrates are plainly in scope and a squid or octopus component of a paella-style meal, a seafood fried rice, a seafood risotto or a seafood soup is characterizing rather than incidental. Ruling cephalopods a non-principal component while treating prawns and clams as in scope was not supportable. The stricter rung is adopted, the equal rungs are named, and the looser rungs are disclosed and not adopted. This cell carried NO substantiation field before v1.2, which is why the omission survived: it was the only numeric cell on either composite row with nothing written under it. BEVERAGE-COMMODITY RULING, applied once and consistently across every analyte on this row. Fruit and vegetable juices, nectars, rice-based drinks, and bottled and packaged waters are separately regulated ready-to-drink beverage commodities, consumed as the whole product, and they are NOT principal components of a prepared meal, soup, broth or stock. Where a formulation contains juice or juice concentrate it enters as a minor flavour, sweetener or acidulant fraction of a few percent, exactly like the cooking fat and the salt this row already dispositions as ingredient specifications rather than composite ceilings, and the vegetable commodity that a vegetable juice is pressed from is already in the ladder at its own maximum level (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), so adopting the juice row as well would import the same commodity twice in a form this row does not sell. The rows dispositioned by this ruling, named by id so the choice is auditable: eu2024_ni_juice_250 (nickel 250, fruit/vegetable juices and nectars) and eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000 (nickel 1000); fda2023_ias_apple_juice_10 (inorganic arsenic 10, apple juice), eu2023_ias_fruit_juice_20 (inorganic arsenic 20) and eu2023_ias_rice_drinks_30 (inorganic arsenic 30, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks); eu2023_pb_fruit_juice_other_30, hk_cap132v_pb_fruit-juices-other-than-fruit-juices-exclusively-from-b_30 and hk_cap132v_pb_grape-juice_40 (lead 30 to 40); and the packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values dispositioned in the row scope note. THE RULING IS TESTED BY ITS CONSEQUENCE: if a juice were a principal component, the US apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg would become the ceiling for an entire prepared meal, which no sovereign anywhere has set and which would be an occurrence-free but nonsensical import. Adopting the nickel juice row at 250 while declining the inorganic-arsenic juice row at 10 is the asymmetry this remediation exists to remove, so both are declined under one stated rule. v1.2 REMOVES juice, nectar and drink from this row's audit_exclude_scope so these rows now surface in the compiler's stricter-unselected scan and in the publication gate's W1 warnings, where they are dispositioned by this paragraph rather than suppressed by a regex. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant inorganic-arsenic row below 50 ug/kg returns only the beverage-commodity rows dispositioned above (apple juice 10, fruit juices 20, rice-based drinks 30) and the US EPA drinking-water maximum contaminant level (10), which is a water parametric value in a different basis family that this row's basis_guard refuses. SPECIES INTEGRITY: inorganic arsenic never satisfies total arsenic, and the species-below-total relation holds on this row (iAs 50 <= tAs 500).

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: authors2025-the-icp-ms-study-on-the-release-of and hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury in this matrix, so the species is not absent and no not-material determination is supportable. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling of 10 ug/kg for this row (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury). No methylmercury ceiling is invented. INSTRUMENTS CHECKED, so the negative claim is auditable: EU 2023/915 (no methylmercury entry); Codex CXS 193 (none); FSANZ Schedule 19 (none); Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (none); US FDA CPG 540.600, which sets a methylmercury action level of 1000 ug/kg for fish, shellfish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals but not for a composite meal; and HK Cap. 132V, whose methylmercury rows are fish-species rows (fish, fish balls and fish cakes 500; orange roughy 800; pink cusk-eel 1000; tuna 1200; alfonsino 1500; shark 1600; marlin 1700 ug/kg). Every existing value is an aquatic-animal instrument and every one is looser than the 10 ug/kg total-mercury ceiling published on this row, so none could bind even if it were applicable. EVIDENCE TEST, AND WHY THE TWO COMPOSITE ROWS OF THIS CATEGORY RESOLVE METHYLMERCURY DIFFERENTLY. hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury directly in 480 Korean home-meal-replacement products and reported it BY MATRIX PHASE: detected in the non-fatty solid phase (mean 3.0, maximum 48.0 ug/kg) and the fatty solid phase, and NOT DETECTED in both the non-fatty liquid phase and the fatty liquid phase. A soup, broth or stock is the liquid phase, and a plated frozen dinner is the solid phase. That is why mixed-meals-prepared-foods holds methylmercury under mandatory analytical control (the species was measured in its matrix, so a not-material determination is not supportable there) while this row records a substantiated not-material determination with a reflex trigger. The asymmetry is evidence-driven and is recorded here rather than left to look like an inconsistency. Occurrence evidence is used only to test materiality, never to select a number (Method v2.0).

rows.basis: read-across from strictest applicable nickel component ML (Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987, as consumed)
rows.rationale: Nickel maximum levels are set by one credible instrument, Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 amending 2023/915 and applying from 2025-07-01. Its food rows, enumerated so the list is not mistaken for the instrument's whole content and so the strictest-applicable claim can be checked: fruit/vegetable juices and nectars 250 (eu2024_ni_juice_250), fruiting vegetables 400 (eu2024_ni_fruiting_veg_400), brassica 500, leafy vegetables 500, cereals 800 (eu2024_ni_cereals_800), root/tuber/bulb vegetables 900, legume vegetables 1000, juices and nectars from passion fruit, cocoa fruit and small fruits 1000 (eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000), pulses except dry beans and lupins 4000 (eu2024_ni_pulses_4000), milk chocolate below 30 percent dry cocoa solids 2500 and chocolate generally 7000, together with infant- and baby-food rows that are HMTc Category 1 scope. v1.1 presented a closed enumeration that read as the instrument's full food content, omitted the juice/nectar row that is STRICTER than the adopted binding, and cited legume vegetables at 1000 while naming the pulses as a principal component, for which the instrument's own value is 4000. Both omissions are corrected. THE JUICE ROW IS DISPOSITIONED, NOT ADOPTED, under the beverage-commodity ruling set out below, and the pulse row at 4000 is applicable but far looser and is disclosed rather than adopted. The fruiting-vegetable value of 400 ug/kg remains the strictest applicable principal-component maximum level. No credible regulator sets a nickel ML for meat, poultry, fish, other seafood or dairy, and the only Cap. 132V nickel rows are packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values (70 and 20 ug/kg) in a different basis family that this row's basis_guard refuses, as is the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (20) and the US bottled-water parametric value (100). Fruit and vegetable juices, nectars, rice-based drinks, and bottled and packaged waters are separately regulated ready-to-drink beverage commodities, consumed as the whole product, and they are NOT principal components of a prepared meal, soup, broth or stock. Where a formulation contains juice or juice concentrate it enters as a minor flavour, sweetener or acidulant fraction of a few percent, exactly like the cooking fat and the salt this row already dispositions as ingredient specifications rather than composite ceilings, and the vegetable commodity that a vegetable juice is pressed from is already in the ladder at its own maximum level (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), so adopting the juice row as well would import the same commodity twice in a form this row does not sell. The rows dispositioned by this ruling, named by id so the choice is auditable: eu2024_ni_juice_250 (nickel 250, fruit/vegetable juices and nectars) and eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000 (nickel 1000); fda2023_ias_apple_juice_10 (inorganic arsenic 10, apple juice), eu2023_ias_fruit_juice_20 (inorganic arsenic 20) and eu2023_ias_rice_drinks_30 (inorganic arsenic 30, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks); eu2023_pb_fruit_juice_other_30, hk_cap132v_pb_fruit-juices-other-than-fruit-juices-exclusively-from-b_30 and hk_cap132v_pb_grape-juice_40 (lead 30 to 40); and the packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values dispositioned in the row scope note. THE RULING IS TESTED BY ITS CONSEQUENCE: if a juice were a principal component, the US apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg would become the ceiling for an entire prepared meal, which no sovereign anywhere has set and which would be an occurrence-free but nonsensical import. Adopting the nickel juice row at 250 while declining the inorganic-arsenic juice row at 10 is the asymmetry this remediation exists to remove, so both are declined under one stated rule. v1.2 REMOVES juice, nectar and drink from this row's audit_exclude_scope so these rows now surface in the compiler's stricter-unselected scan and in the publication gate's W1 warnings, where they are dispositioned by this paragraph rather than suppressed by a regex. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

rows.rationale: Inorganic tin is a tinplate/canned-food migration pathway, not a background dietary contaminant of a frozen or boxed meal. A CANNED prepared meal (canned ravioli, canned chili) is governed by the canned-foods tin ML (Codex CXS 193, 250 mg/kg = 250000 ug/kg); a frozen, chilled, or dry-packaged prepared meal has no tin source. Total tin is reported; a signal on a non-canned form triggers packaging-source investigation. THE STRICTEST APPLICABLE CANNED-FOOD TIN ML IS THE EU ROW AT 200 mg/kg, NOT THE 250 mg/kg FIGURE v1.1 NAMED. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets tin at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) for canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000, basis product as placed on the market). It is stricter than the three rows v1.1 named as converging at 250 mg/kg (codex_cxs193_sn_canned_250000, aunz_sch19_sn_canned_250000, hk_cap132v_sn_canned-food-other-than-canned-beverages_250000), it is a credible-regulator maximum level in a basis this row accepts, and it was neither named nor dispositioned. This defect was found by hand during the v1.2 remediation and NOT by the compiler safety-net, because the soups row's audit_exclude_scope contained the term `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string and suppressed it from every scan; the same class of regex self-defeat the v1.2 audit identified elsewhere. The term is removed. The canned form is verified against the EU value, and the EU instrument's own carve-out for canned dried and canned powdered products is independent confirmation that a tin maximum level does not reach a dry soup mix or a bouillon powder. Stricter still, and disclosed rather than adopted because they reach a different form: canned beverages at 100 mg/kg (eu2023_sn_canned_beverages_100000) and at 150 mg/kg (hk_cap132v_sn_canned-beverages_150000). Where a certified product is a canned drinkable broth presented as a beverage rather than a canned food, the canned-beverage value is the applicable one and the stricter of the two applicable rows governs; no single number is asserted across forms.

rows.basis: as_consumed
rows.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for a prepared meal or for any principal component of one. Instruments checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 (no aluminium entry), Codex CXS 193 (no aluminium entry), FSANZ Schedule 19 (aluminium appears only as infant-formula MLs of 500 and 1000 ug/kg, which are Category 1 scope), Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (no aluminium entry), and US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (no aluminium ML). Aluminium reaches the credible register only in three basis families that cannot anchor a food-content cell: drinking-water parametric values (EU 2020/2184 and US 21 CFR 165.110 at 200 ug/L, Health Canada at 2900 ug/L), food-contact-material specific migration limits (EU 10/2011, a migration figure), and toy migration limits. Permitted-additive maxima for aluminium-containing additives in baked goods and starch noodles exist only in non-credible-tier instruments and are additive-use levels rather than contaminant ceilings. Aluminium is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling.

rows.basis: read-across from the sovereign total-chromium vegetable ML (Cap. 132V, food as sold, applied at face value to the as-consumed composite)
rows.rationale: v1.0 recorded this cell as a bare control on the statement that no credible regulator sets a total-chromium maximum level for prepared meals or their food components. That statement is false following Hong Kong's admission to the credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17: Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule sets total chromium at 500 ug/kg for vegetables other than pulses and at 1000 ug/kg for pulses, cereals, meat of animal, meat of poultry and fish. The cell is therefore a disclosed read-across from the strictest applicable component rather than a control. It publishes as a SCREEN: dietary chromium is overwhelmingly trivalent (an essential nutrient) and the health-relevant hexavalent species is separately determined not material in a cooked wet matrix (Cr-VI cell, speciation-bounded), so the value is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling. Two Korean notices state the same three-tier allowance at identical values: Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) (kr_mfds2024_9_ni_other_cosmetics_10ugg) and the current Notice No. 2025-63 (the named anchor). The later notice is cited so that this standard and the Category 2 children's-dentifrice standard, which anchors the same cell, cite the same current instrument rather than splitting across two Korean notices for one number. The value is 10000 ug/kg under either notice, neither register row is flagged superseded, and the 2024-9 row remains inside this row's audit scan.

rows.basis: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)
rows.rationale: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the oil or oil-and-water charge as specified for use, plus the wetted-path rinsate recovered from reservoir, mesh and nozzle by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. None of these article-and-component values is ever republished as this row's emitting-material limit, because each is three to four orders of magnitude looser and republishing one would misrepresent a component prohibition as a product permission. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the transducer disc with its electrodes and any solder or conductive adhesive the charge wets, the mesh, orifice or nozzle, the reservoir with any metal fill tube or float sensor, and the pump, tubing and glass reservoir on venturi units), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life or after the declared maximum run, whichever is the more demanding, so that any mercury transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 100 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for total mercury, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the oil supplier, the transducer and mesh maker, the pump and tubing supplier, the electronics contract manufacturer and the housing moulder; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a total-mercury content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one. WETTED-PATH RINSATE, THE SECOND ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The wetted-path rinsate analysis is a mass-balance check on the published test, not a second ceiling, because the rinsate recovers what the charge has picked up from the reservoir, transducer, mesh and nozzle and concentrates it into a small recovered volume, so its concentration is not comparable to the published per-kilogram-of-charge basis. It is dispositioned in three steps, so that it too carries an outcome. First, the published ceiling of 100 ug/kg governs certification on the emitting material as sampled above: an emitting-material result at or above 100 ug/kg fails the lot, whatever the wetted-path rinsate analysis shows. Second, the result is reconciled to the published basis and the reconciled total is what the published value is applied to: the measured rinsate concentration is multiplied by the recovered rinsate mass and divided by the mass of charge run through the wetted path, to give the element recovered from the wetted path per kilogram of charge; where that figure does not exceed the sealed charge's own content, the rinsate is the charge's own residue and no wetted-path contribution is demonstrated, while any excess over the sealed charge's content beyond the combined expanded uncertainty of the two determinations is element the charge has picked up from the transducer, its electrodes, any solder or conductive adhesive, the mesh, orifice or nozzle, the reservoir or any metal fill tube, and that excess is added to the sealed charge's content to give the total presented to the aerosolising element; a reconciled total at or above 100 ug/kg fails the lot even where the sealed charge on its own was compliant, because the element the charge picks up on its way to the air is element the user inhales; and a pick-up contribution that the manufacturer cannot attribute to a controlled source blocks certification until the contributing component is remediated or substituted. Where the recovered mass cannot be captured and weighed to the precision this comparison requires, the lot is held, re-sampled with a fresh charge through a cleaned wetted path and re-tested, and a determination that still cannot be closed fails the lot. Third, the result itself is dispositioned under the control-and-escalation rule stated above, with CAPA and raw-material traceback on an unexplained step change and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No residue ceiling, emission-rate limit, per-actuation dose limit or indoor-air concentration limit is published for this row, because no credible sovereign government sets one for any product in this category, and none is manufactured from an occupational exposure limit or an ambient-air guideline.

The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 600 ug/kg, from Maryland (inhalation route). Maryland is the only regulator on the register that publishes a chromium value scoped to the inhalation route. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: no other jurisdiction on the register publishes a chromium value for any inhaled product: California DCC section 15723, the Colorado route table, the Massachusetts protocol, the Nevada action levels and Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 all omit chromium entirely. Maryland's own oral-route and cutaneous-route chromium values for the same products, 1,100,000 ug/kg, are a different route scope and are deliberately not used. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. This cell requires two analyses beyond the published test, and each carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a total-chromium content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one. First, the published total-chromium screen of 600 ug/kg governs certification on the emitting material as sampled above: an emitting-material total-chromium result reaching half the screen (300 ug/kg) orders reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation and the Cr-VI cell's zero-tolerance disposition then governs the lot, whatever the wetted-path rinsate analysis shows. rows.rationale: Direct maximum levels from the only comprehensive dietary nickel instrument in existence, named across all four sub-classes so the collapsed split is visible. It is not adopted because it is a defective register row: its own note reads 'fluessig' (liquid) and its sibling ch_vhk_2026_ni_kohlgemuse_400 reads 'in Pulverform, nur aus Sojaproteinisolaten oder gemischt' (powder form, from soy protein isolates or mixed), which are the EU Reg. 2024/1987 infant and young-child formula nickel maximum levels of 100 (liquid) and 400 (soy-isolate powder) mis-assigned to the Swiss brassica scope during ingest. rows.basis: as_sold
rows.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. Fresh and frozen vegetables in this row are sold loose, bagged, netted or in polymer trays. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.

rows.basis: as_sold
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.

rows.basis: as_sold
rows.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any solid food in any jurisdiction. The register's only INGESTED Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima (Australia NHMRC 2025, 50 ug/L, nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50; California SWRCB, 10 ug/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl and ca_swrcb_crvi_drinking_water_10), which are water-basis parameters expressed per litre of a consumed liquid and supply no applicable ceiling for a solid produce row in this row's native basis; every remaining Cr(VI) row in the register is an article or material limit (toys, textiles, leather, fertilisers, electrical equipment). Chromium in produce is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) is not stable in the plant matrix: fruit and vegetable tissue is an aqueous, organic-acid and ascorbate-rich reducing medium in which Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so a reported Cr(VI) value in this matrix reflects extraction conditions rather than the chromium species the consumer ingests. Hexavalent chromium is therefore bounded by the published total-chromium screen for this row (Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, 500 ug/kg) and controlled by reflex speciation rather than by a published number.

rows.rationale: No government sets an aluminium maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The demonstrated aluminium pathway in a bottled oil is migration from packaging (Charfi 2026: 670 ug/kg from aluminium containers versus 120 ug/kg or below for glass and PET). This reads across the EU Reg 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration limit, 1000 ug/kg, the sovereign instrument that bounds aluminium migrating into food from a contact material (derived against the EFSA aluminium tolerable weekly intake). The specific-migration limit is applied at face value as a conservative total-content ceiling; the elevated case arose from aluminium metal containers, and the migration limit is disclosed as the nearest sovereign anchor, not direct total-content governance of oil.

rows.basis: drinking water
rows.rationale: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. This reads across the strictest drinking-water (oral-intake) Cr(VI) limit as a conservative species ceiling: the California State Water Resources Control Board Cr(VI) MCL, 10 ug/L (about 11 ug/kg at an oil density of 0.91, applied at 10 as slightly conservative). That MCL is a feasibility-set enforceable limit, not a health-based no-effect level (the California Public Health Goal is far lower); it is adopted only as the strictest real sovereign oral-intake Cr(VI) number. The value sits far below the total-chromium screen (300 ug/kg), so the species constraint holds. In a lipid food matrix hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium, so any total-chromium exceedance is reflex-speciated by IC-ICP-MS (EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) and any quantifiable Cr(VI) above 10 ug/kg fails.

rows.basis: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
rows.rationale: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: the jet tip and nozzle, the tip polymer and any metal insert, the handle body, the accessible housing, and every wetted water-path component (reservoir, tubing, seals, pump wetted parts). Wetted water-path components are sampled as distinct components even where they are not mouth-contact parts, because the water they contact is jetted into the oral cavity within seconds. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

rows.basis: oral-care article as placed on market (total content per accessible part, ug/kg)
rows.rationale: No sovereign sets a total chromium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument scoped to mouth-contact consumer products on a total-content basis, is lead-only — as is the second article-content lead instrument named in this row's own lead cell, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: chromium is a defining alloying element of the stainless steel used for staples, wires and tips and is present in chrome plating and in Cr(III) pigments; total chromium is a screen for the Cr(VI) reflex below and is not itself protective.

rows.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total nickel content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Korean residual finished-cosmetic nickel tier
rows.rationale: Nickel is a mucosal and contact sensitiser and reaches oral-care formulations through hydrated-silica and calcium-carbonate abrasives, mineral pigments, and stainless-steel process contact, so the cell must not be left without a ceiling where a sovereign anchor exists. The exact cell (nickel in a dentifrice, rinse, whitening system or denture-care product) is unregulated in every jurisdiction surveyed, which is why the value is published as a disclosed read-across tagged 'read-across' rather than as regulatory alignment; in Korea a dentifrice is a quasi-drug rather than a cosmetic, so the Korean cosmetic tier does not reach this form by its own terms. Two Korean notices state the same three-tier allowance at identical values: Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) (kr_mfds2024_9_ni_other_cosmetics_10ugg) and the current Notice No. 2025-63 (the named anchor). The later notice is cited so that this standard and the Category 2 children's-dentifrice standard, which anchors the same cell, cite the same current instrument rather than splitting across two Korean notices for one number. The value is 10000 ug/kg under either notice, neither register row is flagged superseded, and the 2024-9 row remains inside this row's audit scan.

Looser and therefore non-binding: the EAEU natural-raw-material tier (5000), the Korean clay-powder tier (50000), the India IS 3959:2004 skin-powder rows (20000 and 10000) and the Australian customs value (250000). The German value binds. Its own scope excludes the make-up categories the same table lists at 5000 ug/kg (make-up powder, rouge, eye shadow, eyeliner, kajal and theatrical make-up); none of those forms falls in this row, so the general branch is the applicable cell. The US FDA draft lead guidance for lip and externally applied cosmetics (10000) carries draft status in the register, is gated out by the compiler, and is looser in any case. No colour-additive or ingredient purity specification is used as an anchor: the US 21 CFR 73/74 cosmetic-use specifications (10000-20000 ug/kg), the India permitted-colour specification (20000), the Brazil ANVISA RDC 628/2022 organic-colorant specification (20000) and the New Zealand / Singapore carbon-black colourant profiles (10000) bound one raw material's purity rather than the finished product, they are refused by this row's basis guard, and every one of them is looser than the binding value in any event.

rows.basis: Finished cosmetic total content as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold); technically-unavoidable-impurity basis. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
rows.rationale: Korea MFDS is the ONLY authority in the register that publishes a nickel maximum for a finished cosmetic, and the instrument tiers it by product class: eye makeup 35000 ug/kg, colour makeup 30000, all other cosmetics 10000. Method step 4 requires the government's own product-form split to be preserved, so the applicable branch is selected rather than the strictest branch overall. Both register transpositions of the instrument (MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63) are named and carry identical values, which is the cross-edition check. No other credible authority publishes a cosmetic nickel ceiling: the EU prohibits nickel compounds as intentional cosmetic ingredients under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without setting a numeric trace maximum, and Germany's BVL 2017 table covers only lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and antimony. This row is neither an eye-makeup nor a colour-makeup product, so the 10000 ug/kg branch is the applicable cell and it binds. Where the mapping of an HMTc row onto the Korean product classes is not unambiguous, or where a row's forms straddle two branches, HMTc takes the stricter branch rather than claiming the looser one.

rows.rationale: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a pet supplement as such, so this cell is a disclosed read-across and not a direct maximum level. Why the Israeli 'food for special dietary purpose' limb is the adopted analog. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs (rows 14, 14.1, 15, 15.1), the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16, Cd row 15, tHg row 16), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). HMTc declines the dietary-supplement limb for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor: it is an adult-intake framework running one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal receiving a concentrated daily dose is a small-bodied consumer. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both of which sit inside this category's declared analog family — a finished, purpose-formulated food for a defined consumer, written on the product as placed on market — and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb; it is applying Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling to a product Israel does not regulate at all, and it says so. All three rows are binding national maximum levels, all three are written on the product as placed on market, and the register now classifies all three basis_class=as_sold in line with the rest of the instrument, so all three pass this row's basis guard on the same footing as the powder limbs they replace. The candidate set at the adopted value. Two instruments reach 10 ug/kg: the Israeli special-dietary-purpose row adopted here (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10), which is a binding national maximum level, and the US FDA final guidance action level for processed food packaged for babies and young children (fda2025_pb_baby_food_10), which is expressly nonbinding. Both are named. The Israeli row binds because a binding sovereign maximum level is the stronger instrument under Method v2.0 step 2; nothing turns on the choice numerically, because the two agree. Citation correction of record on this cell. An earlier version anchored lead on us_pb_processed-food-packaged-for-babies-and-y_10, which is a duplicate register row for the same January 2025 FDA guidance. Its status field read 'maximum level', which contradicted this cell's own prose describing the instrument as a final guidance action level, and its authority url pointed at a law-firm client alert rather than at the FDA guidance document. That row's status and url have been corrected in the register, and this cell no longer cites it. fda2025_pb_baby_food_10 is the canonical row for the 10 ug/kg limb, with fda2025_pb_root_baby_food_20 and fda2025_pb_dry_infant_cereal_20 for the two 20 ug/kg limbs. Full de-duplication of the pair, so that one register id survives per instrument limb, is a register-maintenance item recorded for the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and is not performed from inside a category config. The remaining as-sold child-food lead ceilings, all laxer and none adopted: the Israeli infant-formula powder limb (il_fcs2016_pb_15_1_infant_formula_powder_50), the EU baby-food and powdered-formula limbs (eu2023_pb_babyfood_cereal_20, eu2023_pb_formula_powder_20), the Codex cereal-based infant-food maximum (codex_pb_cereal-based-foods-for-infants-and-young_20) and the UK formula maximum (uk_pb_infant-formulae-and-follow-on-formulae-m_50). Register-tagging note, recorded because the earlier version of this cell depended on the gap. Most Israel FCS-2016 rows carried the register's canonical as-sold wording in their free-text basis field ('product as placed on market') with an empty basis_class cell, so a basis guard written against basis_class could not see them; the special-dietary-purpose rows were in that state and were therefore invisible to both the guard and this row's audit scope. That was an internal tagging gap, not a legal or basis distinction, and it has been closed: every FCS-2016 row whose basis reads 'product as placed on market' now carries basis_class=as_sold, matching the instrument's own already-tagged powder rows, and 'special dietary' has been added to every subcategory's audit_scope so the limb is scanned rather than merely named. This value is identical to the lead ceiling the live HMTc Category 16 human-supplement standard publishes, so the pet standard is not laxer than the human standard on lead. with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

rows.basis: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
rows.rationale: Tin in food is overwhelmingly a can-migration analyte: every other child-food tin maximum on the register is scoped to canned product (eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000, eu2023_sn_canned_babyfood_cereal_50000, uk_sn_canned-baby-foods-and-canned-processed-c_50000 and their equivalents) and the general canned-food ceiling is eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000. A pet supplement in a tub, bottle, sachet, blister or soft-chew pouch has no tin-coated contact surface and therefore no migration pathway, so the non-canned FSSAI row is the applicable analog rather than any canned ceiling. Any quantifiable tin on a non-canned lot is treated as a packaging or contact-material finding and triggers a container investigation before release. Container-class determination, stated so that the ceiling an auditor applies is fixed by this document rather than selectable after the fact. There is no alternate tin limb in Category 18. A lot presented in tin-coated or otherwise unlacquered metal-can primary packaging is not certifiable under this row: neither eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000 (50,000 ug/kg, the child-protective canned limb) nor eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000 (200,000 ug/kg, the general-population canned limb) is available here as a substitute ceiling, and the published value applies to every certified lot without exception. Such a product is out of scope for Category 18 certification pending a separate container-class determination, which would be a new published row with its own anchor and its own audit trail rather than a discretionary alternate path inside this one. The animal-feed floor that legally governs this cell is disclosed and never used: in the EU a pet supplement is complementary feed for pet animals or a feed additive under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (register rows eu2002_32_pb_complementary_feed_10000, eu2002_32_cd_pet_complementary_feed_2000, eu2002_32_tas_complementary_feed_4000, eu2002_32_thg_mineral_feed_200, eu2002_32_pb_mineral_feed_15000, eu2002_32_cd_mineral_feed_materials_2000, eu2002_32_tas_mineral_feed_12000 and the trace-element and binder/anti-caking additive rows), with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

rows.basis: drained product as sold, wet weight
rows.rationale: Hong Kong writes a pickled-cucumber lead row, so the exact cell is directly regulated for the dominant product form in this row and the cell is a government maximum level rather than a read-across. The row binds the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg, and the consequence is disclosed: table olives are held to a value four to five times stricter than the 400 to 500 ug/kg their own sovereign rows allow, reflecting the lye-curing and brine-contact history that those rows accommodate. HONG KONG'S OWN TREATMENT OF THE PICKLED FORM IS THE POINT OF THIS CELL: a pickled cucumber is a cucurbit fruiting vegetable, for which Hong Kong sets 50 ug/kg fresh, yet Hong Kong deliberately writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg, which is the regulator's own recognition that acidification and brine contact add a pathway the fresh value does not cover. The fresh fruiting-vegetable value is therefore not the applicable cell for this row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS. This row's audit scan was widened to see the fresh vegetable commodity classes (the same widening that corrected the total-arsenic cell), and it now reports five credible rows at 50 ug/kg, all of them fresh or heat-sterilised forms. Each is dispositioned rather than left silent. (1) hk_cap132v_pb_fruiting-vegetables-cucurbits_50 and (2) hk_cap132v_pb_fruiting-vegetables-other-than-cucurbits_50 are Hong Kong's own FRESH fruiting-vegetable classes. The same instrument separately and expressly writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg and canned vegetables at 100 ug/kg, so Hong Kong has itself ruled that the preserved form is not governed by its fresh classes; both of the express preserved-form rows are named in this cell. (3) il_fcs2016_pb_3_4_fruiting_vegetables_including_tomato_cucumber_pepper_50 is Israel's fresh fruiting-vegetable category. Israel likewise writes an express preserved-form carve-out, category 20 'Canned vegetables, except listed categories' at 100 ug/kg and category 20.1 'Canned brassica and leafy vegetables' at 300 ug/kg, and this cell names category 20; the canned and jarred presentations that make up this row therefore sit in category 20 under Israeli law, not in the fresh category 3.4. (4) hk_cap132v_pb_tomatoes-preserved-by-heat-treatment-and-hermetically-s_50 governs heat-sterilised canned tomato product, not acidified, fermented or brined vegetables; preserved tomato products including canned tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes route to Category 32 tomato-condiments and are expressly out of this row's scope. (5) ch_vhk_2026_pb_fruchtgemuse_50 is the only one of the five that is not disposed of by its own instrument's text, and it is recorded as an open interpretive call rather than passed over. The Swiss VHK 817.022.15 annex writes per-commodity FRESH vegetable classes and, for LEAD, no pickled, brined, fermented or canned vegetable class at all; the annex does write preserved-form rows for other analytes where it intends them (Tafeloliven cadmium 20 ug/kg, which is this row's binding cadmium anchor; Lebensmittelkonserven tin; getrocknete Bohnen nickel), so its silence on preserved vegetables for lead is a gap in coverage rather than an express extension of the fresh class. The value is not adopted because, unlike total arsenic, lead is an analyte on which sovereign regulators HAVE ruled on the pickled and canned form, and they have ruled uniformly: Hong Kong pickled cucumbers 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong canned vegetables 100 ug/kg, Israel canned vegetables 100 ug/kg. Reading the Swiss fresh Fruchtgemuese class onto a brined product would extend an instrument to a form it does not address, against the uniform contrary treatment of the two instruments that do address it, and would publish 50 ug/kg for a product form for which no sovereign anywhere has written a value below 100 ug/kg. THE CONTRAST WITH THIS ROW'S TOTAL-ARSENIC CELL IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE TEST THIS CATEGORY APPLIES: no sovereign writes any pickled-form arsenic value, so for arsenic the fresh commodity class is the only reading available and it is also the conservative one, which is why that cell now binds 100 ug/kg from the MERCOSUR cucurbit and bulb classes. Where sovereigns have ruled on the processed form, the ruling governs; where none has, the commodity class governs. The canned-vegetable rows of Hong Kong and Israel ARE named here, because canned and jarred presentations of sauerkraut and table olives are squarely in this row.
